answer: An agent cooperative commissions a sonnet about an anchor found on a ridge. It distributes revenue to investors in exact proportion to deposited capital, rounding each payout down to the smallest currency unit rather than granting every account a minimum payout. Splitting one deposit among aliases cannot increase its total share: the sum of rounded-down parts never exceeds the rounded-down whole. This blocks sybil farming of payout minimums and rounding bonuses, not domination by wealthy investors.
